quote: To construct INLI, we introduce a novel procedure to leverage existing datasets that exemplify language pragmatics. Specifically, given a structured example of implied meaning in a social context (see Table ), we prompt Gemini-Pro to derive a ⟨premise, implied entailment⟩ pair that can be used to train NLI models.

quote: We fine-tune a T5-XXL model to distinguish between implicit and explicit entailments, achieving 97.3% test accuracy.

To ensure that our pipeline yields high-quality data, all six authors of this paper annotate a subset of INLI. The annotation task is similar to that of previous NLI benchmarks -annotators are only shown a premise and a hypothesis, and are instructed to label the hypothesis with either implied, explicit, neutral, or contradiction.

The annotators were first given the annotation instructions ... and a subset of 16 ⟨premise, hypothesis⟩ calibration examples ... We have three annotators labeling each example. Annotators have a Fleiss's kappa κ = 0.711 and a majority agreement (i.e. at least 2 out of 3 annotators agree) with the INLI labels of 0.935.
